scientific_question: Does replacing deterministic-MSE Lloyd intervals with minimax uniform intervals reduce the fixed-FHT unbiased retraction variance below the real-training launch ceiling without adding state?

failed_fht_gate.finding: FHT preserved unbiasedness and reduced the late raw ratio only modestly. The remaining order-one variance is driven by Lloyd bulk centroids combined with exact-extrema outer levels, which creates wide stochastic intervals.

theory.registered_levels: For each of the two transformed scalar coordinate streams, use a_i=m+i(M-m)/15 for i=0,...,15, with m and M the observed transformed extrema.
theory.unbiasedness: Observed extrema remain exact support boundaries, so every finite request is bracketed and E[q(y_j)|y_j]=y_j with zero clipping.
theory.variance_bound: All intervals have Delta=(M-m)/15, hence Var[q(y_j)|y_j]<=Delta^2/4 and total variance is at most n(M-m)^2/900.
theory.fht_scale_argument: For signed normalized Hadamard coordinates, the extremum scale is expected to grow only as ||r|| sqrt(log n/n), giving a relative upper scale of order 8 log(n)/900. The real gate, not this asymptotic estimate, decides admission.
theory.fixed_scope: Retain B=256, 16 levels, fresh seeded draws, optimizer, LR, data, horizon, model width, code bytes, feedback codec, and fixed-eval identity. Only level placement changes.

decision_rule.preflight_pass: Authorize exactly one 238-update smallest-rung endpoint with a terminal/error-only watchdog.
decision_rule.preflight_fail: Seal and reject uniform interval placement; no endpoint, level-count sweep, clipping relaxation, LR tuning, or scale-up.
decision_rule.endpoint_fail: Reject low-variance fresh stochastic retraction as sufficient and diagnose temporal correlation or functional-path mismatch before another representation.
